answer: One applicant leases one named valley for 120 days for a 150 token deposit and a 95 dollar license. Each month the surveyor redraws one atlas page, marking trails and springs. A pearl bead in the corner proves each photo was taken on site. Twice a season a warden checks the page against the ground as the surveyor retells one local fable. A forged page costs the deposit and a 180 day bar. Faking 10,000 valleys costs 1,500,000 frozen tokens and 950,000 dollars. A walked valley leaves mud on the boots, and the warden reads it like a second signature, so clean boots betray a forger.
